title: French toast
summary: Slices of a quick almond-flour loaf soaked in cinnamon custard and fried in butter until crisp outside and soft inside.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F) and line a 20 × 20 cm (8 × 8 in) pan with parchment.
Whisk the loaf's dry ingredients, then beat in the eggs, melted butter and almond milk. Spread in the pan and bake 20–25 minutes, until firm and golden.
Cool completely — at least 20 minutes — then cut into 8 slices. Warm bread falls apart in the custard.
Whisk the custard ingredients in a shallow dish.
Melt half the butter in a large frying pan over medium-low heat. Dip each slice briefly, about 5 seconds a side; it absorbs fast.
Fry 2–3 minutes per side until golden, adding the rest of the butter for the second batch. Serve hot.
dairy_free_notes: With dairy-free butter and coconut milk the slices brown a little less; fry them over slightly lower heat for longer.
tips: Day-old slices of the almond-flour sandwich loaf work just as well and skip the first step.
Top with a few berries and powdered sweetener.

origin.history: Bread soaked in milk and egg and fried is very old: a Roman recipe collection attributed to Apicius describes it. Medieval Europe knew it by names such as pain perdu, "lost bread", because it rescued stale loaves. "French toast" is an English-language name; the dish itself is common to much of Europe.
